newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Moody's rates Puma Finance Ltd notes.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates Puma Finance Ltd notes.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said it has assigned long-term credit ratings of Aaa to the US$665 million E-1 Series Class A1 and A2 Senior notes issued by Puma Finance Limited.
Moody's said the ratings are based on the level of subordination provided to the senior notes by the E-1 Series 1B subordinated notes equal to five percent of total notes issued.
They are also based on the underlying assets backing the E-1 notes in the form of Masterfund E-1 Certificates issued by Perpetual Trustees Australia Ltd, as Trustee of Puma Masterfund E-1.

Moody's said the ratings also reflect the obligations of the currency swap provider, Morgan Guaranty Trust Company of New York, rated Aa1, to meet U.S. dollar payments to noteholders by taking the Australian currency and exchange control risks through the currency swap agreement.

It added that the ratings are based on the quality of residential mortgage loans held by Masterfund E-1 and the strength of the legal documents setting out the obligations of the various parties in the PUMA Masterfund E-1 programme.
The issuer is a bankruptcy-remote, special purpose company, designed to issue multiple series of note, each backed by series-specific assets.
The programme is managed by PUMA Management Ltd, a subsidiary of investment bank Macquarie Bank Ltd.
